correctness.rationale: A zero leaf would require its sole neighbor to be simultaneously zero for restraint and two for domination. With all leaves positive, the core zero set must induce no isolates. At a positive core, both it and its leaf can take either positive label, independently. At a zero core, the leaf can take either positive label if the core borders a positive core, and must take two otherwise. These factors give the full polynomial, with a unique least-weight term per zero set. For a path with r nonempty zero-core runs and h occupied-complement end runs, b=2r-2+h and n>=3r-1+h. Saturation gives precisely the stated choices: (k,1) at n=3k, (k,2) at 3k+1, and (k+1,0) or (k,2) at 3k+2, the last with one free extra site. Directly, P_1 has one optimizer and P_2 has two. On a proper cyclic zero set, b=2r and n>=3r; distributing n-3k extra sites over 2k alternating runs and marking a start gives the factor n/k and all three residues. The claimed extremal equality requires the complement to consist of a single universal vertex and the induced deletion to have no isolates, and both example families check. The frozen verifier and verification notes were inspected, not executed; the decision rests on the general proof.
